notes: Read all three units, preceding bipartisan foreign-policy context, all eleven candidates and the review. Preserved affirmation as a position, normalized leadership metaphors without changing substance, made the Republican Party the actor in its future undertaking, named both U.S. parties, and contextualized the current President and Secretaries as the 2016 U.S. administration while specifying the displaced consensus.

claims.claim_text: The Republican Party affirms its world-leadership tradition established by President Eisenhower and followed by every subsequent Republican president.
Republican world leadership would act directly and require other countries to contribute.
The Republican Party embraces American exceptionalism and rejects claims of U.S. decline and diminished stature.
The Republican Party says it will lead the world toward a century of greater peace and prosperity.
U.S. presidents from both Republican and Democratic parties had prioritized U.S. interests, friendly governments' trust and Israel's security.
The platform judges that the 2016 U.S. president and his secretaries of state replaced that bipartisan foreign-policy consensus with ineffective posturing.
It judges the 2016 U.S. administration's resulting actions ruinous for everyone except Islamic terrorists and their Iranian and other sponsors.
